AskParams.description:
`agent.ask` params.

**There is deliberately no `agent` field.** The asker is the `PeerRole::Agent` the seam
resolved, never something the sender fills in: the method table grants this method to
`Agent` and to nothing else, and having no sender-supplied `agent` field is the cell that
makes the row safe to grant. [`AgentText`](super::AgentText) is the nearest existing shape and
is what all three of this method's neighbours use — `agent.steer`, `agent.answer` and the
`agent.question` notification — so reaching for it is the natural mistake, and it carries
exactly the field that would let one agent park another in `Wait`.

**`token` is declared here rather than left for the seam to find in the raw params.**
`Presented::token_of` reads the token out of `params["token"]` before dispatch, and every
params type in this module denies unknown fields — so a type that omitted `token` could not
carry one at all: the call would be refused `-32602` before the seam ever looked.
[`HookEventParams`](super::hook::HookEventParams) is the only other params type that declares
one.

text.description:
The question, as the human will read it.

Bounded in **bytes** by `dudes_rpc`'s `MAX_ASK_TEXT_BYTES`, and **refused rather than
truncated**: a truncated question is one whose meaning the daemon changed,
and an append cannot be un-journaled. The bound is deliberately not restated as a schema
`maxLength`, which counts characters — that would put a bound on the wire that the handler
does not enforce.

The rungs of the breaker ladder, in order. The ladder itself — one rung up per beat with a
signal, one rung down per healthy beat, with a bounded compaction exemption — is

BreakerSignal.description:
A signal that raises the breaker one rung on the next beat.

Adding a variant is a minor change, but
declaration order is journal-visible: derived `Ord` sorts the supervisor's per-agent
`BTreeSet` before it becomes `Record::BreakerBeat.signals`.
Therefore append variants; never insert one ahead of an existing variant.

oneOf.description:
The last turn end was `Inferred` (gate 2: `Hold` plus a breaker signal). No v1 emitter
writes such an end — a managed end is `ChildExited` or the reaper's Observed `Vanished`,
attached-mode quiescence is [`Self::PtySilence`] and a hook timeout is
[`Self::HookTimeout`] — and the signal stays because gate 2 stays: `decide()` must not
know which emitters exist.
Attached-mode PTY silence (at most one rung per beat).
The supervisor did not answer a hook within its deadline and the hook server failed open.
A standing steer hit the vendor's consecutive-block cap and blocking stopped at 7.
Five notifications for one mail item went unacknowledged.

A managed turn declared default isolation but its observed vendor init payload reported
inherited plugins or servers.

A managed turn's observed vendor init reported a billing credential source while no
ceiling is set in any scope.

The name states the conjunction on purpose. A billing source is not an anomaly on its own
— it is ordinary for an operator who set a ceiling — so what is wrong is the pair, and a
reader of a `Record::BreakerBeat` is told both halves without a second field to look up.
Raised from observed *configuration* rather than observed *behaviour*, which is what makes
it the first of its kind here.
Repeated fast failures diagnosed from observed exits and duration. Alone raises only Steer.

The boot identity this run stamps every spawn with, or the reason it has none — one field
beside `ping`.

**Why an operator is shown it at all.** The host reads this once at daemon
start and stamps the whole run from the cached value, and the liveness table compares it against
what each recorded key carries. A run whose read failed therefore answers
[`Liveness::Unknown`] to every key that carries a boot identity, for the rest of that run
and with nothing an operator can do to it — the turns stay open, a standing kill defers,
and the loop makes no progress on those agents. That case is nearly unreachable;
nearly unreachable is exactly the class of failure worth seeing before it bites rather than
diagnosing afterwards, and this field is where it is seen.

**Absent means this daemon did not report one** — a reply from before the field existed
(the contract grows by addition) — and never a claim about the host. The three
claims a host *can* make are the three variants, and [`HostBoot`] says why collapsing any
two of them is the defect rather than a simplification.

the probe exchange and the open turns, lost on restart and re-asked on the next start; a
`Done` or a `Stop` taken from it would be an `Inferred` fact reaching a verdict, which
invariant 3 forbids. It is an operator's view and nothing else.

and not proof the vendor stayed under it.

one that survives replay (invariant 1). A defaulted `bool` rather than

therefore no selection.

input_digest.description:
blake3 of the complete canonical decision input, lowercase hex: ordinary `LoopInput`,
or `ClosingLoopInput` during a validated Announced interval before Complete. The
closing input includes closure identity, all ordinary gates, actual task and answers.
The decision is reproducible
from the journal — or the **empty string** when no digest could be produced, which is
the one legal value that is not 64 hex characters.

The sentinel exists because the digest is fallible: an input the serialiser refuses has
no canonical form, and hashing the empty byte string instead would hand every such
decision one well-formed digest they all share. A reader must therefore
treat this as "the input of this decision is not identified" rather than as a hash, and
must not compare it for equality with another decision's digest to conclude the inputs
matched. No writer produces it today — `LoopInput`'s field graph holds no fallible
serialiser — so it is a contract for the case rather than a case in the field.

max_turns.description:

replayed for every launch.

only the provider's behaviour remains. An explicit `0` is refused before the hire is
recorded — it never means unlimited or provider-default — and negative, fractional,
nonnumeric or out-of-range values fail this typed decode as `-32602 InvalidParams`.

**A backstop, not a ceiling.** It is no part of budget admission and no part of hop
accounting. There is no update method in v1: a different value needs a
retire and a rehire.

HostBoot.description:
This run's boot identity, as the host that read it reports it, and the *reason*
when there is none.

**Three values, because two of them mean opposite things and the third is their difference.**
`AdoptionKey`'s `boot` is `Option<String>` and its `None` carries exactly one meaning — the
writer asserts its start value is wall-clock-anchored — and never "the writer is boot-relative
but could not read its boot identity". A host reporting itself has the same two
facts to keep apart, and one more reason to: [`Unreadable`](Self::Unreadable) is the state in
which every recorded key that carries a boot identity answers `Liveness::Unknown` against this
host, so every open turn of that run stops making progress. Collapsed into "this host has
none", that is a failure that is nearly unreachable and invisible; kept
apart, `system.doctor` can say it out loud before it bites.

Declared here rather than in the host or the supervisor because it is on the wire —
`system.doctor` answers with it once per run — and a contract type may not reach into either
([`Liveness`](crate::Liveness) lives here too for the same reason).

**Opaque.** A boot identity is compared for equality and never parsed: a kernel that changes
the format of its value still works. The `String` in [`Unreadable`](Self::Unreadable) is the
opposite — a message for an operator, never compared.

**No `Default`, deliberately.** Every variant is a claim about a host, so there is no value a
deserialiser could supply on a producer's behalf without inventing one: a payload that names no
boot identity is a daemon that did not report one, which is a fact about the *reply* and is
carried by the absence of the field rather than by a variant of this type.

A boot-relative platform whose read failed this run, and what the platform said about it.

Nothing this host spawns is recorded (the spawn is refused rather than writing a key whose
`None` would lie), and every recorded key that *does* carry a boot identity answers
`Liveness::Unknown` here — no evidence, rather than a wrong `Gone`.

Liveness.description:
The host's answer to a probe of a recorded child's *adoption key*.

`Gone` requires positive evidence; anything that is not `Alive` and is not positive evidence of
absence is `Unknown`, never `Gone`. **How a key is compared against a probe is one table,
the liveness table of the supervisor**, cited here and deliberately not restated: it is applied in exactly one function,
`dudes_supervisor::host::liveness`, and only the supervisor decides what an answer means.

It is declared in this crate rather than in the supervisor because it is on the wire —
`system.doctor` answers with it per open turn — and a contract type may not
reach into the supervisor. `dudes_supervisor::host` re-exports it, so the supervisor's own name
for it is unchanged. What the platform layer *read* is a different thing and does not move: a
`ProbeAnswer` is what a host saw, this is what the rule decided, and only the decision is on the
wire.

`Unknown` is a property of a recorded child process and never of a caller. The role a socket
peer resolves to is named `Unproven` where this one would have been ambiguous — a different
word on a different type, so one word never carries two meanings. The classification table in
`dudes_rpc::auth` decides what resolves to that role; it is not restated here.

oneOf.description: A process with that pid exists and its start value equals the recorded one.

Positive evidence of absence: no such pid, a different start value (the pid was reused), or
two *present* boot identities that differ (the machine rebooted).

The host could not answer, or the key and this host disagree about whether a boot identity
exists at all. Nothing is written; the turn stays open and is re-asked.

ModelSelection.description:
The model a managed turn was launched under, as the adapter chose it **before** the spawn.

The selector is the provider's own spelling, kept byte-for-byte: Dudes resolves no alias, keeps
no model catalogue, and never claims this is the model that ran. What actually consumed tokens
is observed at the result boundary and is a different fact with a different cardinality —
`TurnEnded.model_usage`, which may name several models where this names at most one.

**The type exists so that the absent and the empty cases stay distinguishable.** Wrapped in an
`Option` on the record, three states survive replay where a bare `Option<String>` would collapse
two of them: the field absent is a journal written before model selection was recorded and recording no choice at
all; `ModelSelection { selector: None }` is a turn that deliberately took the provider's own
default; `ModelSelection { selector: Some(..) }` is a turn that named one. A re-issue replays
the second and third exactly, and only the first may fall back to current configuration —
which is why flattening the two `Option`s is the mutation the record tests refuse.

It crosses operator configuration, the adapter seam and the journal, so it is shared vocabulary
rather than an adapter-owned type. It carries a `String`, so `Clone + Eq + Hash` rather than
`Copy`, per this crate's own rule.

OpenTurnHealth.description:
What `system.doctor` found for one open turn: a turn the daemon recorded as spawned and has
not closed. The seven fields of the per-turn report, plus the one thing that asked:
[`key_uninterpretable`](Self::key_uninterpretable), which is decided from the host's boot
identity without a probe.

Why the row exists at all. Invariant 3 forbids synthesising a `Gone` out of a probe the host
could not answer, so a turn whose liveness answer stays `Unknown` stays open indefinitely.
That price is accepted on one stated condition — that the operator can
see the stuck turn — and there is a shipped platform on which the
`Unknown` answer is the ordinary outcome rather than an edge. This row is that condition, and
it is the whole of it: see [`DoctorResult::open_turns`] for what may read it, which is nothing.

Not `Copy`, because `boot` owns a `String`. That is the control for [`AgentHealth`]'s derive
rather than an accident of the fields.

The boot identity of the machine the child started on, where the start value is

key_uninterpretable.description:
This host cannot interpret the turn's adoption key **at all**, so no probe of it can ever
answer anything but [`Liveness::Unknown`] while this run lasts.

It is the diagonal of the liveness table — the key and this host disagree about whether a
boot identity *exists*, either because the journal was written on another platform or
because this boot-relative host's own read failed — decided by the one predicate
`dudes_supervisor::host::key_is_interpretable` that `liveness` itself reads, so the marked
set and the stuck set are the same set by construction rather than by agreement.

**Not a synonym for `liveness == Unknown`, and that is the whole of its value.** A host that
could not read the process table this second answers `Unknown` too and recovers by itself;
this one does not recover, and no action available to the operator on this machine resolves
it. `liveness` says what the last probe answered, and this says whether asking again can
ever answer differently.

**A property of the pair, not of the row.** The same recorded key is uninterpretable on one
host and ordinary on the next, so this value is meaningful only beside the
[`boot`](DoctorResult::boot) of the same reply and must never be stored as if it were a
fact about the turn.

`#[serde(default)]`: absent reads as `false`, which is a reply that reported no problem
rather than one asserting there is none.

unknown_for_ms.description:
How long the current run of `Unknown` answers has lasted, in milliseconds.

`Some` only while `liveness` is [`Liveness::Unknown`], and it is the age of the **first**
`Unknown` in the current run, never of the latest one. The distinction is the
whole value of the field: an age taken from the latest answer would reset on every probe
and report a permanently stuck turn as a fresh one for ever. An answer that leaves
`Unknown` clears the stamp, so a later run of `Unknown`s is aged from its own first answer.

The supervisor's own run-local liveness state carries that first stamp. It is in-memory
state and neither a record nor a replay obligation: restart clears it, and the next run
reports no age until its first `Unknown` answer.

oneOf.description: A budget ceiling is reached.
The hop cap is reached.
The agent is halted.
The agent is `Exhausted`.
The provider is managed-only; `agent.attach` is not possible.

The goal has an open turn; `goal.reassign` must wait. `goal.set` refuses with it while the
agent has a turn or a check running in its directory, where the new goal's check would run.
The call presented a token matching no minting, or a retired agent's.

`agent.retire` was called on an agent whose open turn has `Unknown`
liveness (the retirement cannot wait, so the call is
refused rather than deferred).

The agent already has an open question; a second `agent.ask` is refused. A question is open from its `Record::HumanQuestion` until a `Record::HumanAnswer`
for the same agent, and an agent has one slot for one — so a second append would silently
overwrite a question a human may be reading. The refusal is therefore a gate in front of
the append, never a correction applied after it.

**What refuses with this is `agent.ask`** (an agent-only method), in the daemon's `Ask::Ask`
arm: the gate reads the projection's `open_question` on the loop thread, before the
command reaches `persist`, which is the pre-append moment the paragraph above requires.
A well-formed conditioned effect was suppressed or quarantined after its method's `Requirement` admitted the call.

A ceiling is **required** for this call and none is set.

The daemon's own environment carries an environment variable that means a turn on the named
provider can be billed, and the call set no ceiling in any scope or unit — so a managed
child would inherit that credential and run with nothing to stop it but the hop cap. The
refusal is made before the record is written, so a refused `agent.hire` or `goal.set`
journals nothing.

**This is the opposite of [`RefusalGate::Budget`], which is why it is not that value.**
`Budget` means *a ceiling is reached*; this means *no ceiling exists*. A caller branching on
one must never be handed the other. It is not a configuration complaint either: the
configuration can express a ceiling perfectly well and the operator did not give one, and a
missing instruction is not an inexpressible one.

The remedy is any ceiling in any scope — `--usd-per-day`, `--usd`, `--tokens`, or
`[budget] floor_usd_per_day`. **A ceiling of `0` counts**: it is a ceiling the operator set,
and it refuses at the first turn rather than at the hire.

A ceiling exists in a unit whose configured per-turn reserve is zero.

Appended so every earlier variant keeps its derived order and serialized spelling.

The call names no question that is open for that agent: a local `agent.answer`
to an agent with no open question, refused before any record is constructed.

**The opposite of [`RefusalGate::OpenQuestion`]**, which means the agent already has one.
The same spelling is the Floor answer route's reason for the same fact. Appended, for the
reason given above `OpenQuestion`.

A hire's working directory is at, under or above a worktree that is leased to a live agent
or is still being created, or it cannot be placed against the leases. Refused
before any record is constructed. `agent.hire` answers with this gate. The Floor's
onboarding hire is refused as well, with its usual empty 403 and no reason. Appended, for
the reason given above `OpenQuestion`.

A worktree hire cannot be served: this platform or git does not support it, the directory
is no repository, a named lease is unknown or from another repository, or the daemon could
not create the tree. Nothing is left behind and nothing is journaled as an
agent. Appended, for the reason given above `OpenQuestion`.

`goal.set` ran the goal's check once before the first turn and it already passed, so it
cannot show when this goal is done. Nothing is journaled. Appended, for the reason given
above `OpenQuestion`.

`goal.set` ran the goal's check once before the first turn and it timed out or was ended
by a signal, so it shows nothing about the state before work. Nothing is journaled.

`goal.set` could not run the goal's check before the first turn: its directory or program
is missing, the program is inside the tree, or the board card does not exist. Nothing is
journaled.
